name: Orlando
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Orlando: hospitality and tourism diligence, simulation and defense suppliers, Florida litigation support.
hero_lede: Orlando is the most visited destination in the United States and a centre for simulation, defense technology, health care and conventions. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for Orlando matters, using public records and coordinating investigators licensed under Florida's Chapter 493 and counsel where local work is required.
intro: The Orlando metropolitan area had about 2.87 million residents in July 2024, according to the US Department of Housing and Urban Development, and has been among the fastest-growing large US regions. Tourism dominates: a Tourism Economics study for Visit Orlando counted 75.3 million visitors in 2024 and a record economic impact of USD 94.5 billion, with roughly 468,000 jobs tied to the sector. Walt Disney World, AdventHealth and Universal are the largest employers. Orange County also describes the region as a global hub for modeling, simulation and training, with Lockheed Martin and the Central Florida Research Park, alongside aerospace, life sciences, semiconductors and digital media. Orlando International Airport handled more than 57 million passengers in 2024.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Orlando because large volumes of money, people and contracts move through its hospitality, real estate and technology sectors. Investors and lenders need to understand hotel, attraction and property operators and the entities behind them; prime contractors need assurance about simulation and defense subcontractors; insurers face claims arising from a high-volume visitor economy. Rapid population growth brings real estate and construction disputes, while health care expansion raises provider and vendor questions. Florida licenses private investigators under Chapter 493, and its records are kept largely at county level, so work must be scoped carefully and carried out through licensed professionals.

matters.title: Hospitality and attraction counterparty diligence
matters.text: Hotels, attractions, restaurants and vacation property operators in Orlando are often held through layered entities. We research ownership, principals, related companies, litigation and liens so investors, lenders, franchisors and suppliers understand who controls a business before committing capital or entering long-term contracts.

matters.title: Simulation and defense subcontractor checks
matters.text: Orlando's simulation and training cluster supplies defense and aerospace programmes. We help prime contractors and investors review subcontractors for ownership, foreign connections, litigation, debarment and adverse media, supporting supply chain and compliance requirements without accessing restricted government systems.

matters.title: Visitor-economy insurance claims
matters.text: A visitor economy of more than 75 million people a year produces liability, property and travel-related claims. We provide background and asset research on claimants, providers and businesses involved, and coordinate Florida-licensed investigators where surveillance or witness interviews are required.

matters.title: Real estate and construction disputes
matters.text: Rapid growth in Central Florida drives residential, commercial and hospitality construction. We assist counsel with developer and contractor histories, related entities, construction liens, prior litigation and witness backgrounds across Orange, Osceola, Seminole and other relevant counties.

matters.title: Health care provider and vendor research
matters.text: Large health systems are among Orlando's major employers. We support compliance teams and counsel with research on practices, clinics and suppliers, covering ownership, licensing and disciplinary history, litigation and exclusion lists, within federal and Florida privacy limits.

local_context.title: Florida investigator licensing
local_context.text: Chapter 493 of the Florida Statutes requires a licence from the Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services, through its Division of Licensing, to perform or advertise private investigation for pay. Individuals hold Class C licences, interns Class CC and agencies Class A. Unlicensed activity is a first-degree misdemeanour, and repeat violations a third-degree felony with civil penalties up to USD 10,000. TDSC coordinates Florida-licensed investigators for local work.

local_context.title: Courts serving Orlando
local_context.text: State civil cases arising in Orlando are heard by the Ninth Judicial Circuit Court, covering Orange and Osceola counties. Federal cases go to the Orlando Division of the US District Court for the Middle District of Florida, with appeals to the Eleventh Circuit in Atlanta. Counsel decides the forum; TDSC tailors research on parties, witnesses and corporate histories to the case. Many dockets are available online, with access rules varying by record type.

local_context.title: Records and registries
local_context.text: Florida business entities are registered with the Department of State's Division of Corporations, whose public records generally list officers or managers and registered agents. Deeds, mortgages and liens are recorded by county clerks or comptrollers, so Orlando research typically covers Orange County and often Osceola and Seminole. We confirm the counties connected to each person or company before searching. Online access differs by county.

local_context.title: Simulation and research cluster
local_context.text: Orange County identifies modeling, simulation and training as a global specialism, centred on the Central Florida Research Park, which has more than 9,500 workers and 140 companies focused largely on military simulation. Work involving this sector often raises export control, government contracting and foreign ownership questions that counsel must assess; our role is factual research using lawful public sources. Federal exclusion records are a standard starting point.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Orlando and works on Orlando matters from Nashville. We first agree the purpose with counsel, whether Ninth Judicial Circuit or Middle District of Florida litigation, diligence on a hospitality or simulation-sector counterparty, an insurance claim or judgment enforcement, and scope the research to it. Sources include Florida Division of Corporations filings, Orange, Osceola and Seminole County official and court records, federal dockets and exclusion lists, regulatory actions and media. We do not access restricted government systems. Any surveillance, interviews or other local work in Florida is carried out by investigators licensed under Chapter 493, within the scope we agree.

faqs.q: Does an investigator need a Florida licence to work in Orlando?
faqs.a: Yes. Chapter 493 of the Florida Statutes requires a licence from the Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services to perform or advertise private investigation for pay, with criminal penalties for unlicensed activity. TDSC is not licensed in Florida and coordinates Florida-licensed investigators for any local work, with counsel confirming requirements.

faqs.q: Which county records matter for Orlando research?
faqs.a: The City of Orlando lies in Orange County, and the metro area extends into Osceola, Seminole and Lake counties. Deeds, liens and court records are maintained county by county, so we identify the counties connected to the person or business and search them rather than relying on a single index.

faqs.q: Can you vet a simulation or defense subcontractor in Orlando?
faqs.a: We research a subcontractor's ownership, principals, foreign connections, litigation, federal exclusion records and media from lawful public sources. We do not access classified or restricted government systems, and export control or contracting conclusions remain for the client's counsel. Findings are documented with sources and confidence levels.

faqs.q: Can you research hotel or vacation property owners in Orlando?
faqs.a: Yes. Orlando hospitality and vacation properties are often held through limited liability companies. We combine Florida corporate filings, county property and lien records, litigation and other states' registries to identify likely controlling individuals and related assets, stating where ownership cannot be confirmed from public records.

faqs.q: Where are business disputes heard in Orlando?
faqs.a: State disputes are heard by the Ninth Judicial Circuit Court for Orange and Osceola counties, and federal cases by the Orlando Division of the Middle District of Florida. Counsel decides the forum and strategy; we support with research on parties, witnesses, related companies and assets suited to the proceedings.
